status: FINAL · delta check Sun 22 Nov 19:06 Bucharest · no correction, Phase 1 scores confirmed
summary: Fear is back (risk mood −2: stocks −9% in 4 weeks, VIX 35.9): safe havens gain, high-yield currencies lose.
Strongest: USD (+7). Weakest: CAD (−7) after oil fell 21%; NZD −2, JPY −1.
EUR and CHF climb to 0; AUD and GBP slip to 0; gold factor turns positive (+1).
key_events: Wed 25 Nov 15:30 · US GDP and PCE inflation (USD, XAU) — HIGH
Thu 26 Nov · US Thanksgiving; French budget committee (EUR)
Fri 27 Nov · Tokyo CPI (JPY); NZ election result (NZD); S&P France review (EUR, date unconfirmed)

USD.name: US dollar
USD.breakdown:
`R1 +1` · `R2 +1` · `R3 +1` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 +1.0`
Raw **+6.75** → Published **+7**
Priced-in: **Partially priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **High**
why: Fed officials keep asking for more rate hikes. On Friday Governor Cook said waiting longer risks falling "behind the curve". A December hike is about 92% expected, but bets on January slipped, so the market may still be too low (judgement: without it the score would be lower).
Core retail sales beat forecasts (+0.6% vs +0.4%), a hawkish surprise.
Stocks fell about 9% in four weeks and the fear gauge (VIX) jumped to 35.9. In fear, money goes to the dollar, so it gets a small safe-haven bonus.
USD.helps: Core PCE (25 Nov) at or above 0.3% m/m and Fed speakers pushing January or 50bp.
USD.hurts: Fed officials linking the equity rout to a slower pace, or December pricing falling below ~85%; a soft core PCE.
events: 25 Nov US Q3 GDP (2nd) and October PCE (core cons +0.3% m/m) (HIGH)

EUR.name: Euro
EUR.breakdown:
`R1 0` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 +1` · `N2 −1` · `G1 0`
Raw **−0.45** → Published **0**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Oil fell about 21% in four weeks. Europe buys its energy abroad, so cheaper oil helps.
France's extra borrowing cost over Germany is smaller than a month ago (155bp vs 172bp), so the budget worry counts less.
The ECB is expected to raise rates in December (about 91%), but that is already in the price.
EUR.helps: A French budget compromise at the CMP and a calm S&P review (27 Nov), with the spread below ~145bp.
EUR.hurts: The spread back above ~165bp, a failed CMP with 49.3 talk, or an S&P downgrade on 27 Nov; oil rebounding above $105.
events: 26 Nov French PLFSS joint committee (CMP; expected this week, date not confirmed) (HIGH)
27 Nov S&P rating review of France (date not confirmed) (HIGH)

GBP.name: British pound
GBP.breakdown:
`R1 +1` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 −1.0`
Raw **0.00** → Published **0**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: UK data were mixed: inflation on forecast, jobless rate lower, but fewer people on payrolls.
The Bank of England is about 80% expected to raise rates in December. Good interest rate, but the pound loses a bit when markets are scared.
GBP.helps: MPC speakers (Pill 23 Nov, Greene 24 Nov, TSC 25 Nov) backing December and more; strong flash PMIs.
GBP.hurts: December BoE pricing falling clearly below ~70%, or a deeper equity rout.

JPY.name: Japanese yen
JPY.breakdown:
`R1 −1` · `R2 −1` · `R3 −2` · `N1 +1` · `N2 +1` · `G1 +2`
Raw **−1.35** → Published **−1**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Two Japanese numbers disappointed: growth shrank and core inflation was 2.2% vs 2.3% expected.
Markets still expect a December BoJ hike at about 86%. With weak data, that bet looks a little too high (judgement call: without it the score would be +2).
Supports: cheaper oil, government warnings against a weak yen, and safe-haven buying when stocks fall.
JPY.helps: Tokyo CPI (27 Nov) above the 3.1% forecast, Ueda (30 Nov) or Tamura (26 Nov) confirming December, or actual intervention.
JPY.hurts: BoJ speakers hedging on December, December swaps falling below ~70%, or a sharp risk-on rebound.
events: 27 Nov Tokyo November CPI (mkt 3.1%; time not verified) (HIGH)

CHF.name: Swiss franc
why: Switzerland pays 0% interest, which usually weighs on the franc.
But fear is high (VIX 35.9), and the franc is a classic safe place, so the two cancel out.
We found no market price for the next SNB decision, so this score has low confidence.
CHF.helps: The risk-off deepening (VIX staying above 30) or an SNB hint at a 2027 hike.
CHF.hurts: A quick risk-on rebound (VIX back under 25) or SNB intervention talk against franc strength.

CAD.name: Canadian dollar
CAD.breakdown:
`R1 −1` · `R2 0` · `R3 −1` · `N1 −2` · `N2 −1` · `G1 −1.0`
Raw **−6.75** → Published **−7**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Medium** · Conviction: **High**
why: Oil (Brent) fell from about $117 to $92.57 in four weeks. Canada sells oil, so this hurts.
Canadian inflation was lower than expected (3.1% vs 3.2%); a December Bank of Canada hike is now only about 40% expected.
No trade deal with the US yet, and the US tariffs stay.
CAD.helps: Macklem (24 Nov) sounding hawkish, an OPEC+ cut on 29 Nov lifting oil, or a written US–Canada deal.
CAD.hurts: Brent below $88, a dovish Macklem, or new US tariff action.
events: 24 Nov BoC Governor Macklem speech (Economic Club of Canada) (HIGH)

AUD.name: Australian dollar
AUD.breakdown:
`R1 +2` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 0` · `N2 0` · `G1 −2`
Raw **0.00** → Published **0**
Priced-in: **Largely priced** · Confidence: **High** · Conviction: **Low**
why: Australia lost 43,500 jobs in October (a gain of 25,000 was expected). Markets now expect no more hikes and some rate cuts by 2027.
Wages grew faster than expected, which softens the blow.
Australia still has the highest interest rate, but the Aussie is the most sensitive to fear, so the stock sell-off hurts it most.
AUD.helps: October CPI (25 Nov) above 4.8% headline / 3.6% trimmed, with the RBA pushing back on cuts; risk-on rebound.
AUD.hurts: A soft CPI that pulls cuts forward, or deeper risk-off.
events: 25 Nov Australia October monthly CPI (mkt 4.8% y/y; trimmed 3.6%) (HIGH)

NZD.name: New Zealand dollar
NZD.breakdown:
`R1 0` · `R2 0` · `R3 0` · `N1 +1` · `N2 0` · `G1 −2`
Raw **−1.80** → Published **−2**
Priced-in: **Not applicable** · Confidence: **Low** · Conviction: **Low**
why: The RBNZ is almost fully expected to raise rates in December, and dairy prices held up.
The final election result comes on 27 Nov; the government's one-seat majority could be at risk.
The kiwi is sensitive to fear, and fear is high.
NZD.helps: An official result (27 Nov) confirming the majority, strong Q3 retail sales (23 Nov) or the next GDT auction rising.
NZD.hurts: Special votes removing the majority, a weaker GDT, or deeper risk-off.

XAU.name: Gold
why: Gold's own ingredients turned slightly positive: fear in markets and central banks buying gold.
Against it: US real interest rates rose over four weeks and inflation expectations fell.
Gold fell about 9% in the week, mostly forced selling. Gold's score = its own ingredients (+1) plus the dollar's score (+7).
XAU.helps: ETF inflows returning and real yields falling with a soft core PCE.
XAU.hurts: More forced selling (ETF outflows) and real yields rising again on hawkish Fed news.
events: 25 Nov US Q3 GDP (2nd) and October PCE (core cons +0.3% m/m) (HIGH)
